text: Ibrahim Rugova, born on 2 December 1944 in Crnce, Istok to a family from the Kelmendi Albanian clan, was a Kosovo-Albanian politician, scholar, and writer who served as President of the partially recognised Republic of Kosovo from 1992 to 2000 and as President of Kosovo from 2002 until his death on 21 January 2006. He founded the Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK) in 1989, which gained the support of 90% of the ethnic Albanian population and advocated for Kosovo's independence through peaceful means. The LDK established a shadow government that provided education and health care to the Kosovo Albanian population, effectively creating a parallel state, which was funded by the overseas diaspora primarily in Germany and the United States. Rugova was elected President of this parallel state in May 1992 and later, in March 2002, became President of Kosovo under a United Nations administration, a position he held until his death. He is referred to as Ati Kombit ("Father of the Nation") in Kosovo and the Gandhi of the Balkans due to his non-violent resistance strategy. He graduated from the University of Prishtina in 1971 and earned a doctorate in 1984 after studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in Paris under Roland Barthes. He was active in civil rights movements, edited student publications, and served as president of the Kosovo Writers Union in 1988. Rugova emphasized the historical heritage of ancient Dardania to strengthen Kosovo's identity and promote Western ties. He was married to Fana Rugova and had three children. As president, he maintained a policy of non-violent resistance despite the rise of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), which advocated armed resistance. In 1998, he secured a second term, but his influence waned as the KLA gained prominence. He participated in the failed Rambouillet talks in 1999 and was taken prisoner by Serbian authorities during the NATO-led aerial campaign, later exiled to Rome in May 1999 and returned to Kosovo in July. While nominal president, effective power rested with the United Nations administration, and in 2000, he and Hashim Thaçi agreed to step down and work on provisional self-government. Rugova was re-elected president in 2002 and again in 2005. He died from lung cancer in January 2006 and was buried on 26 January without religious rites, attended by an estimated half a million people. His grave in Prishtina is oriented perpendicular to Mecca, in accordance with Muslim tradition. Although rumors circulated that he converted to Catholicism, these were unconfirmed and refuted by his family and associates, including Sabri Hamiti, who described him as a 'symbolic Muslim.' The Chancellor of the Catholic Church of Kosovo, Don Shan Zefi, stated there was no evidence of his conversion or baptism. Rugova remained a prominent figure, winning a landslide victory in the 2000 elections with 58% of the vote, and in 2004 appointed Ramush Haradinaj, former KLA commander, as Prime Minister. He faced an assassination attempt on 15 March 2005 but escaped unhurt. He was known for wearing a silk neckscarf, giving visitors rock samples, and being a chain-smoker. He received medical treatment in Germany and the United States before returning to Kosovo, where he continued advocating for peaceful independence and close relations with the U.S. and European Union.
